question: It was recently reported that the Commission wants to declare areas of the KujawskoPomorskie, Łódzkie, Mazowieckie, Warmińsko-Mazurskie and Wielkopolskie provinces that have a high density of poultry farms to be areas with a ‘high risk of the spread of avian influenza’ in order to implement ‘exceptional measures’ that would ban exports and poultry restocking, and would require the slaughter of hundreds of thousands of birds.

The potential ban would apply not only to poultry producers, but also to hatcheries and egg producers. The avian influenza virus (HPAI) is seasonal and its prevalence in Poland does not deviate from the EU average. As weather conditions improve in spring the virus naturally becomes less active.
However, the Commission is proposing that devastating restrictions be introduced just as the epidemiological situation is on the verge of improving. 1.

Since when has the Commission been in discussions with Poland’s central and regional governments on emergency measures to combat avian influenza in Poland? Please indicate the subject of these discussions.
What precise measures does the Commission intend to take in Poland to combat avian influenza? Please include the timelines, scope and entities covered by these measures.
Will the Commission also impose restrictions on trade in the domestic market? Please indicate which products will be affected, as well as what form the restrictions will take.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (6.8.2025) The Commission follows closely the status of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in the EU. From 1 January 2025 until 26 May 2025, Member States have notified 244 outbreaks of HPAI in poultry establishments and more than 12,6 million poultry have been affected in those outbreaks.

Poland notified 85 HPAI outbreaks in poultry establishments1 representing 35% of the EU’s total number of outbreaks. More than 8 million of poultry have been affected in the infected establishments in Poland, that represents 63,5% of the total number of poultry affected in the HPAI outbreaks in the EU.

The Commission is paying special attention to this serious situation and keeps regular contact with the Polish authorities, in particular as regards disease control measures. Poland has faced specific difficulties with the control of the disease in certain areas of high density of poultry establishments.

As consequence of that situation, following technical discussions with the Commission, the Polish competent authorities are implementing certain additional reinforced national measures in the zones of concern aiming to contain disease spread.

These measures were presented at the Standing Committee of Plants, Animals Food and Feed2 and they operate within the framework of EU rules3, including regionalization measures where movement restrictions apply. In view of the evolution of the disease situation, the Commission adopted several Implementing Decisions4 that lay down restrictions, amending the Annex to Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/24475.
